Directive (EU) 2023/970

EU Pay Transparency Kit for SMEs.

The Pay Transparency Directive changes how employers set and talk about pay: pay ranges for candidates, no questions about pay history, answers to pay requests within two months, and pay gap reporting for larger employers. This kit helps you prepare.

Directive (EU) 2023/970

What's in the kit

  • Pay Policy & pay-setting criteria — gender-neutral pay rules ready to adapt and share with staff
  • Recruiter & Manager Guide — what to say, and never ask, in job ads, interviews and pay talks
  • Job Architecture & Pay Ranges — score every role on skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions
  • Pay Data — pseudonymised pay records with automatic total and hourly pay
  • Pay Gap Calculator — the gap per category with an automatic 5% warning
  • Information Requests — employee requests with an automatic two-month deadline
  • Step-by-step compliance plan, filterable by company size
  • Ready-to-use texts — job ad pay wording, annual staff notice, reply to a pay request, contract clause

The rules it covers

  • Before hiring (Art. 5)

    Candidates must get the starting pay or pay range, and you may no longer ask about their pay history.

  • Right to information (Art. 7)

    Employees can ask for their pay level and the average pay of colleagues doing equal work, by gender. You answer within two months.

  • Pay gap reporting (Art. 9)

    From June 2027 for employers with 150+ staff, from 2031 for 100+. A gap of 5% or more that you cannot justify triggers a joint pay assessment.

Made for

  • Employers in the EU, from about 10 staff
  • HR and payroll teams
  • Recruiters and hiring managers
  • Managing directors preparing for national law

Questions about this kit

When do the rules apply?
Member states had to transpose the directive by 7 June 2026. Your national law sets the exact start date, and several countries are still finishing theirs. The kit is built on the directive, and the country editions note the national state of play.
We have fewer than 100 employees. Does this affect us?
Yes. Pay transparency for candidates, the ban on pay history questions and the right to information apply to all employers. Only gap reporting depends on size.
What does the pay gap calculator do?
It calculates the gap per category of workers from your pseudonymised pay data and flags any gap of 5% or more, the threshold that matters under the directive.
